September 7, 1940

The Commissioner

Present.

Dear Sir ,

Mr. Avramow , Manager , of Messrs. Thomas Delarue &
Co. Ltd. of 12 the Bund is now in Mexico-City and wishes to
enter U.S.A.

The American Consulate at Mexico-City is telegraphing
to the Shanghai Municipal Police for police records concerning
the honourability and standing of Mr. Avramow.

Mr. Avramow is a member of a distinguished family and
his Firm is internationally known in the manufacturing of bank
notes. I , myself recommend him unreservedly in every respect.
Mr. Avramow has resided in Shanghai about 15 years.

Should the American Consulate at Mexico-City telegraph
to you I request that you cable back your answer by cable and
any expenses entailed I shall be glad to refund to you.

I also request that you issue a certificate concerning
the honourability and standing of Mr. Albert J. Avramow and if

shall be very grateful to you as I would like to hand it over

Avramow, refused to work with Hendriks and requested that Avramow
return to Shanghai. He hinted that he could not guarantee
further business and even threatened that he was in a position
to cancel orders already received. Mr. Lamert, however,
definitely stated that Avramow would not return to Shanghai in
the capacity that he had formerly held and indicated that upon
arrival in London he would find that his services were no longer
required.
        After remaining in Shanghai for several weeks, Lamert left
for London, where his presence was required in connection with
certain trouble concerning Avramow.
        On February 15, 1932 Mrs. Avramow (still known as Miss
A. Balykoff) returned to Shanghai from America and confirmed
information, which had already been received, to the effect that
Avramow, who had been successful in obtaining several important
orders for his erstwhile employers, had been re-engaged by Thos.
de la Rue & Co. Ltd. and re-appointed Shanghai representative.
        Hendriks, it should be mentioned here, left Shanghai for
London on February 2, 1932 having been recalled, it is alleged,
owing to his incapacity and the influence of Lo in having Avramow

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, JUNE 19, 1933

POSTAL OFFICIAL
IMPEACHED
Control Yuan Denounces Action
of Former Director

Nanking, June 18.
The Control Yuan has brought up
a second impeachment against Mr.
Lin Shih, formerly Director of the
Postal Department of the Ministry
of Communications, for alleged cor-
ruption and other unlawful actions.
In its petition of impeachment
submitted to the National Govern-
ment, the Control Yuan recalls that
when Mr. Wang Po-chun was Minis-
ter of Communications, Lin, who
was then Director of the Postal De-
partment, was impeached by the
Yuan for dereliction of duty in con-
nection with a proposed contract
with certain foreign interests for
the printing of Chinese postage
stamps. To escape punishment, the
petition alleges, Mr. Lin not only
fled to Tientsin for refuge but even
caused an obituary notice to be
published in the papers announcing
his death.
When General Chen Ming-shu be-
came Minister of Communications,
he was, however, "resurrected" and
was again appointed Director of the
Postal Department. "Such an un-
precedented fact is really a blot
upon officialdom," the Control Yuan
says.
The Yuan concludes by urging
that Lin be immediately suspended
from his present post as Director
of the Navigation Bureau at Tin-
tsin and that the matter be referred
to the Official Disciplinary Com-
mittee for immediate investigation.
—Kuo Min.

邮政官员
遭弹劾
监察院谴责前局长之行为

南京，6月18日电。
监察院对交通部邮政总局前局长林世先生提出第二次弹劾，指控其涉嫌贪污及其他违法行为。
在向国民政府提交的弹劾书中，监察院回顾称，当王伯群担任交通部部长时，时任邮政总局局长的林氏曾因在与某些外国势力签订中国邮票印刷合同一事上玩忽职守而遭到该院弹劾。弹劾书称，为逃避惩罚，林氏不仅逃往天津避难，甚至还在报纸上刊登讣告，宣布自己死亡。
然而，当陈铭枢将军出任交通部部长后，他却“死而复生”，并再次被任命为邮政总局局长。监察院称：“此种前所未有之事实，实为官界之污点。”
监察院最后敦促立即暂停林氏目前在天津航政局局长一职，并将此事移交公务员惩戒委员会立即调查。
——《国民新闻》

Subject (in full) Anonymous information to Customs re arrival of alleged counter-
feiter named Auranow.

Made by C. D. I. MacDermott. Forwarded by C. D. I. MacDermott.

Sir,
On 28-3-32 Mr. Sluse, Chief Tide Surveyor, Customs, received
anonymous information by letter that an international counterfeit-
er was arriving by the "Empress of Canada" on 29-3-32 with false
plates.
The letter was written on Hongkong & Shanghai Hotel note-
paper and stated that a Mr. Albert Auranow, a Bulgarian Jew, and
known to the writer as an international counterfeiter, was arriving
on the "Empress of Canada"; that he had false plates concealed in
the covers of books and albums in his luggage with the intention
of operating here. Also, that the writer would identify himself
and claim a reward if the Customs made the seizure. As a means
of identifying himself the writer had cut diagonally through the
crest on the note paper, leaving half of the crest showing, the
production of the remaining half being his identification.
Special arrangements were made by Mr. Sluse to have the sus-
pect's person and luggage searched. In co-operation with Supt.
Woodfield, River Police, I arranged to have D. S. Beloshenko
present at the search. Whatever Police action might be considered
necessary resulting from the search was to be taken by the River
Police.
On 29-3-32 D. S. Beloshenko with D. S. Masikoff, Boarding
House Section, attended the "Empress of Canada" with Insp. Bridges
of the River Police but the suspected person was not on board.
It was ascertained that a Mr. A. J. Auranow, Bulgarian, travelled
1st Class from Vancouver booked to Kobe, and had disembarked at
Yokohama on 26-3-32. This person was known to the purser of the
"Empress of Canada" as a business man who travelled once a year
from Vancouver to the East.

主题（全称） 关于据称名为 Auranow（音译）的伪造者抵达的匿名情报致海关。

制作人 C. D. I. MacDermott。 转发人 C. D. I. MacDermott。

先生，
1932年3月28日，海关首席潮汐测量员 Sluse 先生收到一封匿名信，信中称一名国际伪造者将于1932年3月29日乘坐“加拿大皇后号”轮船抵达，并携带伪造印版。
该信写在香港饭店的信笺上，信中称一名名为 Albert Auranow 的保加利亚籍犹太人（写信人称其为国际伪造者）将乘坐“加拿大皇后号”抵达；他将在行李中的书籍和相册封面内藏匿伪造印版，意图在此地作案。此外，写信人表示，如果海关查获赃物，他将现身并领取赏金。作为身份识别方式，写信人斜向切开了信笺上的徽章图案，留下一半徽章可见，出示剩余的一半即为其身份证明。
Sluse 先生已做出特别安排，对该嫌疑人的身体及行李进行搜查。经与水警督察长 Woodfield 合作，我安排侦探警佐 Beloshenko 在场监督搜查。因搜查结果而可能认为有必要采取的任何警务行动，将由水警执行。
1932年3月29日，侦探警佐 Beloshenko 会同寄宿公寓组侦探警佐 Masikoff，与水警督察 Bridges 一同登上“加拿大皇后号”，但嫌疑人并未在船上。
经查实，一名名为 A. J. Auranow 的保加利亚人乘坐头等舱从温哥华出发，目的地预订为神户，并于1932年3月26日在横滨下船。“加拿大皇后号”的大副认识此人，知道他是一名每年从温哥华前往东方一次的商人。
